episode01-desktop-1440-masthead.mastheadText: girl power meets machine power Episode#01 On Wednesdays We Do AI A gentle first tab for women with full calendars, high standards, and no patience for beige AI explanations. June 3, 2026
episode01-desktop-1440-masthead.readerKit: The Lesson AI fluency starts with one useful, low-risk rep. The gap is not confidence. It is time, context, and tools that were never explained for women already carrying too much. Try-On Open one AI tool, give it a small real task, compare the answer to your own judgment, and notice what would make it more useful next time. This Week's Rule Get in, loser. We're learning AI. Ten minutes counts when it is pointed at a real thing you actually need.

episode02-mobile-390-top.title: LAiDIES #2: Tell Me What You Want
episode02-mobile-390-top.h1: Episode 2: Tell Me What You Want
episode02-mobile-390-top.signoff: Remember, LAiDIES: The Spice Girls didn't say "tell me what you vaguely want, what you sort of generally want." And neither should you. Be specific. Be bold. Be David Rose about it. The LAiDIES Challenge Got a better “Remember, LAiDIES:” sign-off that would make Dolly proud? Post it in the Try-On Debrief. The one with the most likes can get featured later, with credit. We're trAIlblazers here, not idea thieves. If this resonated, send it to a woman who'd get something out of it.

episode03-mobile-390-masthead.mastheadText: Episode 03 The Burn Book Problem AI judgment, hallucinations, and why polished output still needs receipts.
episode03-mobile-390-masthead.readerKit: The Lesson How to check, challenge, source, and contain AI output when it sounds confident but may be wrong, missing context, or not relevant to the real work. Try-On Use a low-risk work task or source notes, run Prompt Like Elle in your own AI tool, then verify at least three claims before using it. This Week's Rule I can use the draft. I still check the alibi.
